episodes.213319: A weak mid level shortwave moved through during the afternoon initiating a few strong storms which produced scattered wind damage reports in western MA.
episodes.213387: A disturbance ahead of a larger scale system over the western U.S. resulted in the development of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms across north central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon hours. High based showers and thunderstorms resulted in brief severe wind gusts at the Las Vegas and Raton Crews Municipal Airports. Showers and thunderstorms exited east into West Texas during the evening hours.
episodes.213495: Thunderstorms developed across the region during the afternoon and evening hours on Tuesday (6/30) due to hot temperatures and unstable conditions. The strongest storms produced wind damage and large hail up to ping pong ball size as they tracked through northeast and east-central Wisconsin.
episodes.213664: A strong mesoscale convective system of thunderstorms dropped southward out of Ontario into Central NY, moving into an unusually unstable and sufficiently sheared environment. This supported severe thunderstorms with widespread damaging winds, an isolated EF1 tornado, and hail. Heavy rainfall also occurred as deep moisture surged northward from the Ohio Valley.
episodes.213842: A surface boundary was in the vicinity of the combined Panhandles through the afternoon and evening hours of June 29th. This combined with daytime heating, ample instability and enough dry air in the higher levels of the atmosphere to bring scattered showers and thunderstorms to the region. Some of these storms intensified to be severe with damaging winds being the primary hazard.
episodes.213846: The surface boundary that was present on June 29th continued to remain across the region into the 30th. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed again on the afternoon and evening of the 30th. Damaging winds were the primary hazard with these storms are enough dry air aloft was able to bring down stronger winds in any robust thunderstorm.
episodes.213847: The surface boundary that was present on June 29th continued to remain across the region into the 30th. Additional showers and thunderstorms developed again on the afternoon and evening of the 30th. Damaging winds were the primary hazard with these storms are enough dry air aloft was able to bring down stronger winds in any robust thunderstorm.
episodes.214132: On the afternoon of the 29th, a dryline moving eastward stalled out around the Interstate 27/US Highway 87 corridor. Strong heating along the boundary created an unstable atmosphere and storms were able to form. A lack of deep layer shear kept storms from becoming organized and led to pulse type thunderstorms. However, one storm did produce a severe wind gust near Floydada (Floyd County).
episodes.214134: A weak dryline formed during the day of the 30th and mixed eastward to the edge of the caprock. Convergence along the dryline, a weak short wave trough, and very hot temperatures contributed to convective initiation by mid-afternoon across the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle and northern Rolling Plains. Storms repeatedly trained over Hall County producing intermittent severe winds gusts near Lesley (Hall County) for over an hour. Late in the afternoon additional thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico in the drier air and moved eastward into the South Plains. A very dry sub cloud layer allowed these storms to produce several severe wind gusts as they marched eastward towards the Interstate 27/US Highway 87 corridor. By the time storms reached Lubbock County late in the evening, they were moving very slowly which produced heavy rainfall over the city of Lubbock (Lubbock County). Numerous city roads on the south side of the city of Lubbock were inundated with water.
episodes.214162: Similar to June 28th, pulses in the southwesterly flow aloft coupled with upslope flow yielded shower and thunderstorm development, starting in the higher terrain and spreading northeastward towards the Trans-Pecos and Permian Basin. A few storms produced severe downburst winds.
episodes.214358: Scattered diurnal convection developed across the Texas Panhandle into far western Oklahoma in the afternoon and early evening of the 30th. A severe downburst was captured by a broadcast media storm chaser northwest of Elk City, OK.
episodes.214474: Clusters of strong thunderstorms along the coast produced a few measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.214526: On June 29th, 2026, severe weather fueled by record humidity and high temperatures impacted the Duluth County Warning Area, leading to 27 total warnings across northeast Minnesota and northwest Wisconsin. Two waves of severe storms swept through the area, producing golf ball-sized hail (1.75 inches), damaging straight-line wind gusts to 60���65 mph, several reported funnel clouds, and one tornado in central St. Louis County during the overnight round of storms. The severe winds uprooted trees, damaged structures, and knocked down power lines across multiple counties.
episodes.214569: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms swept over Lake Superior in late June as minor disturbances pivoted around a mid-level ridge over the southeastern CONUS. These disturbances caused multiple incidences of thunderstorm-driven outflow and gusty winds on Lake Superior from the afternoon of the 29th to the early morning hours of the 30th.  A strengthening low level jet and wake lows trailing the thunderstorms resulted in additional periods of gusty winds, above gale force.
episodes.214607: As a significant ridge was over the southeastern US, hot and unstable air was over Michigan's Upper Peninsula by the 30th. This warm and moist air caused unseasonable heat impacts, and forcing from an approaching upper level disturbance over the Canadian Prairie initiated thunderstorms that caused multiple forms of severe weather, including the first confirmed tornado for the Upper Peninsula since 2020.
episodes.214614: An isolated severe storm brought wind damage and hail to a small area in Dale county.
episodes.214662: A typical summertime pattern produced scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms with isolated severe weather reported.
episodes.214974: A low pressure over the Northern Plains, combined with a moist and unstable air mass, led to a conditional threat of severe thunderstorms as an upper level jet streak moved over North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon along a quasi-stationary surface trough that was placed across central North Dakota. Numerous large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts were reported across southwest and central North Dakota through the afternoon and evening as storms moved through. The largest hail reported was 2.25 inches in diameter in Max in McLean County. The strongest wind gust was also measured in McLean County, with a 77 mph wind gust reported at a US Air Force Weather station just south of Max.
episodes.215180: Isolated thunderstorms fired on the evening of the 29th, with intensity provided by an expanding, but not overly suppressive, high pressure ridge. One storm was able to produce both damaging thunderstorm winds and large hail.
episodes.215276: A strong capping inversion broke along a frontal boundary during the early evening of June 29. With MLCAPE from 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of up to 50 to 60 knots, isolated stronger storms developed quickly across Nebraska and moved across the Missouri River into far southern South Dakota with up to quarter size hail.
episodes.215278: As a mid-level wave moved out of Nebraska toward southeast South Dakota during the overnight, convective clusters blossomed near and ahead of a frontal boundary with MUCAPE from 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of up to 50 knots. Initial, more isolated storms produced hail across northeast Nebraska up to golf ball size, but quickly evolved into bowing segments with damaging wind gusts from 60 to 80 mph across northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.
episodes.215280: As a mid-level wave moved out of Nebraska toward southeast South Dakota during the overnight, convective clusters blossomed near and ahead of a frontal boundary with MUCAPE from 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of up to 50 knots. Initial, more isolated storms produced hail across northeast Nebraska up to golf ball size, but quickly evolved into bowing segments with damaging wind gusts mainly from 60 to 90 mph across northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.
episodes.215281: As a mid-level wave moved out of Nebraska toward southeast South Dakota during the overnight, convective clusters blossomed near and ahead of a frontal boundary with MUCAPE from 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear of up to 50 knots. Initial, more isolated storms produced hail across northeast Nebraska up to golf ball size, but quickly evolved into bowing segments with damaging wind gusts mainly from 60 to 85 mph across northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.  At one point, there were around 600 customers without power due to downed lines and poles in parts of Jackson county.
episodes.215299: Severe thunderstorms including several supercells developed over parts of eastern ND and northwest MN during the afternoon and evening, with very large hail and severe winds reported over parts of eastern ND. The largest hail was the size of softballs in south Fargo, ND.
episodes.215300: Severe thunderstorms including several supercells developed over parts of  west central and northwest MN during the afternoon and evening period, with very large hail and severe winds reported. One supercell produced 3 inch hail in Moorhead, MN. One EF-0 tornado developed with a supercell in Clay County 6 miles northwest of Hawley.
episodes.215317: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced damaging wind gusts in Buncombe County.
episodes.215406: During the evening of June 29, 2026, into the early morning hours of June 30, severe thunderstorms moved across northern and eastern Nebraska, producing hail, damaging wind gusts, and a brief tornado. Storms developed along a cold front within a highly unstable air mass characterized by MLCAPE values exceeding 3,500 J/kg, DCAPE values over 1,500 J/kg, and steep lapse rates.||Two distinct rounds of severe weather impacted the area. The first round targeted far northeast Nebraska���primarily Knox and Cedar counties���between 5:00 PM and 8:00 PM CST. This initial round was dominated by a supercell that produced measured wind gusts up to 60 mph and hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter.||A second round of storms developed in east-central Nebraska later in the evening and tracked northeastward. This activity quickly consolidated into a severe convective cluster that produced damaging winds, hail, and a brief tornado as it passed through Boone, Madison, Stanton, and Wayne counties. The complex intensified rapidly upon entering Madison County and the Norfolk area, producing widespread wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph. A personal weather station 2 miles southeast of Hadar recorded a peak gust of 101 mph, which destroyed a well-anchored carport. Multiple hail reports between 1.00 and 2.00 inches in diameter were also received. A brief, EF-0 tornado was also confirmed in Stanton County, with maximum estimated wind speeds of 85 mph. The system continued northeast into the overnight hours, producing severe wind gusts into northwest Iowa and southern Minnesota.
episodes.215504: A strong complex of storms, or a mesoscale convective system, tracked through eastern New York from northwest to southeast in the afternoon through the early evening of June 30th, 2026. Strong to damaging wind gusts caused widespread tree and powerline damage as numerous bowing segments cycled through the main line. Numerous reports of wind damage were relayed to NWS Albany from 911 call centers and local law enforcement in Herkimer, Hamilton, Fulton, Montgomery, Saratoga, Schenectady, Albany, Rensselaer, and Columbia Counties. However, particularly hit hard was Montgomery County where extensive tree and wire damage was reported across portions of Fonda and Fultonville.
episodes.215505: A strong complex of storms, or a mesoscale convective system, tracked into western Massachusetts from northwest to southeast in the early evening of June 30th, 2026. Strong to damaging wind gusts downed some trees and wires in Lanesborough and Savoy, according to the reports of local amateur radio operators.
episodes.215522: On June 30, 2026, an oppressive tropical airmass fueled by extreme heat warnings collided with a sharp mid-level shortwave across the NWS Buffalo CWA, prompting the Storm Prediction Center to issue a Severe Thunderstorm Watch as strong boundary-layer destabilization produced widespread severe convection across Central New York and the North Country. NWS Buffalo Area Forecast Discussions highlighted surging moisture and extreme instability that unleashed powerful multi-cell clusters and isolated supercells, leading to severe straight-line microbursts with winds up to 100 mph and an EF-1 tornado touchdown in Lewis County. Concurrently, deep warm-cloud processes and precipitable water levels approaching 2.0 inches fueled torrential precipitation efficiency, driving Weather Prediction Center Excessive Rainfall concerns for localized flash flooding in poor-drainage areas. As the pre-frontal convective line swept east toward nightfall, loss of daytime heating and post-frontal drying rapidly stabilized the region, bringing an end to the severe weather threat into the overnight hours.
episodes.215652: A surface cold front moved in from the Dakotas and converged on a very warm and unstable airmass. Dew points had reached the mid to upper 70s with a few pockets of 80 degrees. Although daytime heating was slightly stifled due to afternoon cloud cover, storms developed along the surface front on the evening of June 29th across western MN. A few cells produced large hail and damaging wind gusts in Pope, Douglas, and Todd Counties.
episodes.215654: A thunderstorm complex that had developed over northeastern Nebraska and western Iowa moved into southwestern Minnesota during the overnight hours of June 29th into June 30th. A cold front had stalled across western MN which left a warm and unstable airmass in place over SW MN, helping maintain this complex over several hours. As the complex reached the MN/IA border, wind gusts reached 60 to 70 mph, ultimately causing damage to a maintenance shed and downing trees in St. James (Watonwan County). The strongest thunderstorm wind gust was recorded 1 mile NNE of Welcome at 67 mph.
episodes.215706: During the evening hours on the 30th, a few clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms moved northeast across portions of west-central and northwest Kansas. An 81 mph wind gust was measured in Wichita County.
episodes.215737: During the morning hours on June 30th, a storm briefly intensified and produced golf ball sized hail in Independence, Wisconsin.
episodes.215742: A weak surface trough over the northern peninsula and adjacent coastal waters focused morning convection over the north and central offshore waters producing a waterspout near Anna Maria Island.
episodes.215805: Dissipating convection from the eastern Texas Panhandle produced a notable (and prolonged) heat burst event in Roger Mills County, Oklahoma during the late evening of the 29th.
episodes.215997: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved over Lake Ontario in the evening hours.

NWS survey started where there was sporadic tree damage in Pittsfield and south for a few miles before reaching an area that had much more concentrated damage. A narrow corridor of damage was found just off County highway 46 a few hundred yards into the |woods. This concentrated area of damage followed the road. Accounts of residents helped confirm that this was likely a tornado. Damage became more sporadic downhill towards Elm Grove and State Route 51, but was still in line with the damage |observed already. In West Laurens, the amount of tree damage picked up, likely from outflow winds in town. Headed south of town down Crawford |Road, the damage became more concentrated once again. Many of the |trees along and east of Crawford road were also falling in a southwest |direction with tree damage not concentrated and more random. |West of Crawford, another concentrated corridor of tree damage was found, with vortex intensifying as it crossed a large, open yard before it headed into the forest once again. |Over the top of the hill, the broken off trees continued down |past a lake where the significant tree damage quickly came to an |end. With the lack of any damage corridors or trees falling in a convergent|pattern after this point, this was found to be the end of the |track.

A thunderstorm initiating in southern Marquette County continued to develop into a supercell thunderstorm as it moved east into Delta and Alger County. As the thunderstorm began splitting, the southern segment intensified and produced a weak, EF-0 tornado south of Trenary, MI in Delta County. The tornado crossed Alger Delta 43rd road and proceeded northeast before dissipating.
